title: Normalized exceptional formula on finite coefficient restrictions
statement: Fix a finite-field datum D, a prime l different from D.p, an algebraic closure Omega of Q_l of an independent universe, separated finite-type D.k-schemes X and Y, a separated finite-type D.k-morphism f:X to Y, a compactification c, specified common-stage dualities BX and BY as in [def-sf-common-stage-verdier-data], and a coefficient-compatible exceptional system S at the auxiliary small closure as in [lem-sf-constructible-exceptional-adjunction-coefficients]. For each finite coefficient field E in Omega there is a RationalOperations.ExceptionalIdentification for the actual S-operation and the specified finite BX and BY dualities. Whiskering its finite exceptional comparison with inclusion, BX.comparison, the inverse BY.comparison and the inverse pullback object comparison gives a natural isomorphism from finiteRight_E followed by inclusion_X,E to inclusion_Y,E followed by BY.dual.rightOp, pullback.op and BX.dual. These local isomorphisms satisfy the scalar square of FiniteExceptionalFormula with the actual finiteRightScalar and inclusionTransition maps, including repeated fields. No descended exceptional functor or adjunction is asserted.

proof.text: Use the integral evaluation-defined exceptional comparison and rationalExceptional_identifications with the specified finite dualizing data, Hom identifications and normalized scalar extensions. Choosing its adjunction transpose fixes the finite comparison independently of the scalar partner. The existing finite scalar mate identity then holds for this one family, with its transported adjunctions.

Whisker by the prescribed inclusion and the two duality inclusion comparisons, using inverse BY and inverse pullback object comparison in the contravariant factors. Naturality gives a finite-source natural isomorphism and expanding its component gives the normalized equation. Expand its scalar square, substitute the finite exceptional scalar identity, then the BX and BY scalar squares and the pullback scalar square. Reassociate by naturality and cancel inverse comparisons to obtain the displayed scalar equation. Identity scalars and zero objects obey the same equations.
